nodes.name: TiO₂ support synthesis
nodes.procedure: 5 g TiCl₃ was mixed with saturated NaCl solution (13 g). The mixture was heated to 100°C for 12 h to obtain the TiO₂ support. The solid TiO₂ precursor was collected by centrifuging and washing with ultrapure water for 3-5 times. It was then dispersed in 100 mL ultrapure water in a flask.

nodes.name: Pt/TiO₂ impregnation
nodes.procedure: It was then dispersed in 100 mL ultrapure water in a flask, and then 4 mL 0.01 M H₂PtCl₆ was injected to get a mixture suspension. The suspension was heated to 80°C for 3 h in a water bath. When the solution reached to room temperature, centrifuged and washed 3-5 times with ultrapure water, after which the final Pt/TiO₂ product was obtained by freeze-drying for overnight.

nodes.name: Pt/TiO₂-OVs reduction
nodes.procedure: To prepare Pt/TiO₂-OVs catalyst, the mixture of Pt/TiO₂ and NaBH₄ (mass ratio 1:2) was heated to 350°C and kept for 3 h under N₂ flow in a tube furnace, and the sample was centrifuged and washed 3-5 times with ultrapure water and then freeze-dried overnight.

nodes.name: TiO₂-OVs synthesis
nodes.procedure: The TiO₂-OVs catalyst was obtained by the same method as Pt/TiO₂-OVs synthesis (step 3): the mixture of TiO₂ support and NaBH₄ (mass ratio 1:2) was heated to 350°C and kept for 3 h under N₂ flow in a tube furnace, and the sample was centrifuged and washed 3-5 times with ultrapure water and then freeze-dried overnight.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/TiO2-OVs exhibits two distinctive EPR signals at g values of 1.970 and 2.002, assigned to Ti3+ and OVs respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1a shows the EPR results, where Pt/TiO2-OVs exhibit two distinctive EPR signals at g values of 1.970 and 2.002, which are assigned to Ti3+ and OVs, respectively

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/TiO2-OVs shows Pt 4f peaks at 71.3 eV (4f7/2, low-valence Pt) and 72.3 eV (4f7/2, Pt(II)); Ti 2p shifts 0.19 eV lower indicating Ti3+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Pt 4f XPS spectrum of the Pt/TiO2-OVs can be further deconvoluted into a low-valence state of Pt species 71.3 eV of 4f7/2) and a Pt (II) species (72.3 eV of 4f7/2)

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/TiO2-OVs shows uniformly dispersed single isolated Pt atoms; lattice fringes bending with Ti-Ti distances of 0.266 nm and 0.281 nm indicate local lattice distortion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. S10 clearly shows the uniformly dispersed white dots on the surface of the support, most of which are single isolated atoms

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt loading in Pt/TiO2-OVs is 0.77 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: we determined the Pt loading in Pt/TiO2-OVs is 0.77 wt% by ICP-AES

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping shows homogenous distribution of Pt, O, and Ti throughout Pt/TiO2-OVs particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDX spectroscopy elemental mapping shows the homogenous distribution of Pt, O, and Ti throughout the entire surface of Pt/TiO2-OVs particles

nodes.characterization_summary: Increased pre-edge peaks in Pt/TiO2-OVs indicate severe distortion of local TiOx structure due to OVs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The increase of pre-edge peaks in the Pt/TiO2-OVs is ascribed to the severe distortion of local TiOx structure

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/TiO2-OVs shows lower intensity for Ti-O shell peak indicating lower Ti-O CNs and increased disordering in Ti-O-Ti shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Pt/TiO2-OV shows a much lower intensity for the Ti-O shell peak than that of Pt/TiO2, indicating lower Ti-O CNs

nodes.characterization_summary: Remarkable decrease in white line intensity for Pt/TiO2-OVs suggests less electron holes in Pt 5d orbitals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: there is a remarkable decrease in the intensity of the WL for Pt/TiO2-OVs, suggesting less electron holes residing in Pt 5d orbitals

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/TiO2-OVs shows Pt-O peak at ~1.9 Å (elongated by 0.15 Å vs Pt/TiO2) with lower Pt-O CNs; no Pt-Pt shell confirms atomic dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: a clear positive peak shift (~0.15 Å) could be seen for the Pt/TiO2-OVs, indicating a longer Pt-O bond length

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt/TiO2-OVs particles range 100-200 nm; HRTEM shows 0.35 nm lattice spacing for TiO2 (101) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Pt/TiO2-OVs catalyst shows the size of most particles ranging between 100 and 200 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM confirms 0.35 nm lattice spacing corresponding to (101) plane of anatase TiO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) shows that the lattice spacing is about 0.35 nm, which corresponds to the (101) plane

nodes.characterization_summary: Eg mode peak at 150-160 cm-1 shifts to higher wavenumber in Pt/TiO2-OVs indicating local structural changes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peak at 150-160 cm-1 corresponding to the Eg mode of TiO2 (anatase) in Pt/TiO2-OVs shifts to a higher wavenumber

nodes.characterization_summary: Decreased pre-edge intensity in Pt/TiO2-OVs indicates weak covalence of Ti-O bond due to Ti3+ and OVs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to Pt/TiO2, the decreased pre-edge intensity (the dashed area) of Pt/TiO2-OVs indicates weak covalence of the Ti-O bond

nodes.characterization_summary: Decreased intensity of Ti L-edge peaks in Pt/TiO2-OVs implies reduction from Ti4+ to Ti3+ and decreased Ti-O covalence.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The decreased intensity of Ti L-edge peaks in Pt/TiO2-OVs implies the slight reduction from Ti4+ to Ti3+ and the decreased covalence between Ti and O atoms
